matters.title: 3. RESOLUTION NO. R-15-24 - A RESOLUTION WAIVING PUBLIC BIDDING AND AUTHORIZING SELECTION OF SOLE SOURCE GIS SOFTWARE PROVIDER.
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Mar 12, 2024 - Regular Council Meeting 
 Category 
 N. Regular Agenda 
 Subject 
 3. RESOLUTION NO. R-15-24 - A RESOLUTION WAIVING PUBLIC BIDDING AND AUTHORIZING SELECTION OF SOLE SOURCE GIS SOFTWARE PROVIDER. 
 Type 
 Regular Agenda, Action, Resolution 
 Preferred Date 
 Mar 12, 2024 
 Absolute Date 
 Apr 15, 2024 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 30,900.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 GIS Software Budget - 510-5800-51880-4155 
 Recommended Action 
 Staff recommends authorizing the Mayor to enter the Esri Small Municipal and County Government Enterprise Agreement to maintain the services provided by the existing GIS software installation, to support increased user licensing demand, to meet new server requirements of planned business systems, and to waive public bid requirements in line with Procurement Policy 1.107.130. 

 Since the inception of the GIS Program prior to January 2021 the City of Pullman has used the Esri ArcGIS platform and purchased software and user licenses on a piecemeal basis. Successful growth of the program has meant that the existing licensing is no longer sufficient for current use and anticipated growth. 

 The cost of continuing to purchase the required software and licenses in a piecemeal fashion will exceed the cost of the enterprise agreement negotiated with Esri, the software vendor. 

 Funds budgeted in 2024 cover the cost of the first year of the agreement. Funding for the remaining two years would be addressed in the 2025-2026 budget process ( Procurement Policy 1.107.130 ). 

 Implementation of GIS at the City of Pullman has transformed the way we use data to monitor city resources, make data-driven decisions, and communicate. The program's successful growth has meant that the existing licensing is insufficient for current use and anticipated growth. 

 The City of Pullman GIS provides desktop mapping and analysis software to power users, provides GIS data and map servers to integrated business systems, and provides a web portal for users to view, create, and analyze spatial data to more effectively manage City resources under their care, and provides mobile GIS applications so field crews can maintain operational views of systems under their care. 

 The benefits of the SGEA include: 

 Unlimited desktop licenses for growing numbers of users producing high-quality maps and maintaining complex data sets such as utility networks, land parcel fabrics, and road condition asset management. 

 Additional server licenses to support existing business system integrations as well as new servers for anticipated roles in asset management software. 

 Sophisticated analytic tool licenses that expand return on investment made in creating data. 

 Reduced costs of license administration. 

 Expanded access for users of the WebGIS to create and maintain spatial information. 

 Funds for an SGEA were allocated during the 2023-2024 budgeting process. Esri has offered the City of Pullman a ramped entry into the SGEA three-year commitment at considerable savings. 

 *Staff Contact for this Agenda Item: Sam Jenkins, GIS Administrator 

 *Contact Email: sam.jenkins@pullman-wa.gov 

 Motion & Voting 

 Staff recommends authorizing the Mayor to enter the Esri Small Municipal and County Government Enterprise Agreement to maintain the services provided by the existing GIS software installation, to support increased user licensing demand, to meet new server requirements of planned business systems, and to waive public bid requirements in line with Procurement Policy 1.107.130.

Motion by Ann Parks, second by Megan Guido.

 Final Resolution: Motion Carries

 Yea: Ann Parks, Pat Wright, Megan Guido, Eric Fejeran, Carla De Lira, Trymaine Gaither

 Budget Source

 Recommended Action 
 By motion, authorize the execution of a Sole Source Contract with Gooch Thermal Systems Inc. for a replacement Heat Exchanger for Wastewater Treatment Plant. 

 At their August 9, 2022 City Council meeting , Council authorized and designated Gooch Thermal Inc. as the sole source provider for the Primary Digester Heat Exchangers at the Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP) in accordance with the procurement procedures contained in Pullman City Code 1.107.110(3). 

 A capital improvement project to replace the aging heat exchangers at the WWTP has been approved and is budgeted for 2024. The heat exchanger provides heat for the digestion process needed to meet State of Washington Department of Ecology biosolids permit requirements. It is important that the city maintain the time and temperature requirements via the digestion process, so the biosolids can be disposed of each year. The only direct replacement option for the heat exchanger is the Gooch model 1000K by Gooch Thermal Systems Inc, which is the current heat exchanger model. In order to use a different heat exchanger make and model, the piping and pump configuration at the plant would need to be redesigned and reconstructed, which would be far more expensive and time-consuming than replacing the existing heat exchanger with the same make and model. 

 Attached is a quote for purchasing the heat exchanger from Gooch Thermal Systems Inc. of Whitehall, PA. 

 Staff recommends a motion to approve the sole source purchase of a replacement heat exchanger that is identical to the existing heat exchanger and authorize the Mayor to execute a contract with Gooch Thermal Systems, Inc. 

 Cost Summary: 

 Equipment: $59,000 

 Shipping: $3,240 (20% added for contingency) 

 Tax: $4,917 

 Total: $67,157 

 *Staff Contact for this Agenda Item: Trevor Cook, WWTP Supervisor 

 *Contact Email: Trevor.Cook@Pullman-WA.gov 

 Motion & Voting 

 By motion, authorize the execution of a Sole Source Contract with Gooch Thermal Systems Inc. for a replacement Heat Exchanger for Wastewater Treatment Plant.

Motion by Ann Parks, second by Nathan Weller.

 Final Resolution: Motion Carries

 Yea: Ann Parks, Nathan Weller, Pat Wright, Eric Fejeran, Carla De Lira

matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Jan 28, 2025 - Regular Council Meeting 
 Category 
 N. Regular Agenda 
 Subject 
 1. ORDINANCE NO. 25-01 - AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF PULLMAN, COUNTY OF WHITMAN, WASHINGTON, VACATING A PORTION OF HOPKINS COURT AND ANDRUS DRIVE ADJACENT TO LOTS 4 AND 5 OF THE PORT OF WHITMAN COUNTY INDUSTRIAL PARK SUBDIVISION NO. 2. 
 Type 
 Action, Ordinance 
 Preferred Date 
 Jan 28, 2025 
 Absolute Date 
 Jan 28, 2025 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 -27,684.05 
 Budgeted 
 No 
 Budget Source 
 General Fund 
 Recommended Action 
 By motion adopt the Ordinance to vacate of a portion of Hopkins Court and Andrus Drive. 

 During the previous Public Hearing Agenda Item (M-1), the City Council received input on the vacation of a portion of Hopkins Court and Andus Drive. This Ordinance is presented if the City Council is prepared to take action on that request. 

 On October 8, 2024, Kara Riebold, Executive Director for the Port of Whitman County submitted to the Pullman City Clerk a petition to vacate a portion of Hopkins Court and Andrus Drive right-of-way adjacent south and west boundary lines of Lots 4 and 5 respectively of the Port of Whitman County Industrial Park Subdivision No. 2, which are owned by the petitioner, the Port of Whitman County. The requested vacation and associated legal descriptions are shown in Exhibit “A” of the attached ordinance. The property proposed for vacation is part of an obsolete truck and fire department turnaround from when this section of right-of-way was the terminus for NE Hopkins Court. 
 The current petition to vacate was signed by all parties and therefore represents 100% of the parcel frontage along the proposed street vacation. 
 The area proposed for vacation is about 5,544 square feet, and it abuts Lots 4 and 5 of the Port of Whitman County Industrial Park Subdivision No. 2, which are owned by the petitioner, the Port of Whitman County. The subject property is located in an industrial zoning district. If the subject property is vacated, there would remain a full 60-foot right-of-way width for this portion of Hopkins Court and Andrus Drive. Thus, city staff support the petitioners’ vacation request. 
 City staff investigated existing city and franchise utility locations and determined that various utility lines are located within the vacation area. To accommodate the utility lines and any future utilities, an easement will need to be retained that will allow the use of the property for utility facilities. In addition, due to the lack of sidewalks along the area proposed for vacation, staff recommend that a pedestrian access easement also be retained. 
 The Planning Commission considered this proposal at their November 12, 2024 meeting, addressing the various issues associated with right-of-way vacations. For reference a copy of the staff report to the planning commission is attached. Following it’s discussion the Planning Commission unanimously approved a motion to find the petitioners’ request consistent with the City’s Comprehensive Plan so long as the city retains easements for utilities and pedestrian access. 
 City Code provides that the City be compensated for vacated property at a rate not to exceed the appraised value of the area being vacated. Typically, this value has been determined by Public Works staff using assessed valuations for property abutting, and in the vicinity of, the right-of-way being vacated. The analysis for this proposed vacation has determined an assessed valuation of $9.9870 per square foot. Because the subject right-of-way was dedicated less than 25 years ago (dedication occurred on January 16, 2001), the amount to be charged for the vacation should be 50% of the appraised value. Therefore, the proposed amount to be charged for this vacation is $4.9935 per square foot. The total compensation to the City, based on this rate, for the vacation area is $27,684.05. For reference, a copy of the valuation worksheet for this proposed vacation is attached. 
 *Staff Contact for this Agenda Item: Edward Ranck-Copher, PLS, City Surveyor 
 *Contact Email: edward.ranck-copher@pullman-wa.gov 

 Motion & Voting 

 By motion adopt the Ordinance to vacate of a portion of Hopkins Court and Andrus Drive.

Motion by Pat Wright, second by Carla De Lira.

 Final Resolution: Motion Carries

 Yea: Ann Parks, Nathan Weller, Pat Wright, Megan Guido, Eric Fejeran, Carla De Lira

 Recommended Action 
 By motion, authorize the fire department to purchase advanced medical training equipment from Laerdal using the Sourcewell contract pricing. 

 As part of the 2025-2030 capital improvement plan, the fire department received approval to purchase new medical training equipment to enhance our emergency medical training capabilities. 

 In accordance with the City of Pullman procurement policies, the fire department staff obtained quotes for the hardware and software necessary to provide the desired medical training. Laerdal is the sole source manufacturer for the SimBaby manikin and has a sourcewell contract in which the City of Pullman is a member. The pricing includes instructor training as well as a maintenance and defect warranty. 

 Currently, the Fire Department does not have a simulation baby that can be utilized for in-depth medical training. Also, high-risk, low-frequency events involving the airway require advanced training hardware to provide a realistic simulation to EMS providers. The ongoing training is required by the State of Washington and our medical program director to ensure the providers can provide advanced life support procedures.

 Recommended Action 
 Approve a motion to authorize the contract with Spare Labs, Inc for cloud-based dispatch and scheduling software, training and support for use in Pullman Transit's Dial-A-Ride system. 

 Pullman Transit's current Dial-A-Ride scheduling software is more than a decade old and includes network access requirements that no longer meet technology best practices. Staff have solicited quotes for a replacement package, and recommends the Spare Platform by Spare Labs, Inc (Exhibit A). The Spare Platform allows easy transfer of patron and vehicle trip history from the former software package, as well as daily trip efficiency adjustments to better manage our On Time Performance and Dial-A-Ride patron experience. Driver communication with Dispatch will still be via a mobile data terminal in the vans, but rather than a proprietary hardware screen it will be with a locally provided tablet and the same cellular plan as the former units used. The annual cost is set, and spread over five years. 
 *Staff Contact for this Agenda Item: Wayne Thompson, Transit Manager 
 *Contact Email: wayne.thompson@pullmantransit.com
